# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 77 (Bu-Vb Pc77)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc77
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 77
**Title (English, from literature):** Intentionally making a monk anxious
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 77, titled *Sañcicca* ("Intentionally making a monk anxious"), is a monastic precept from the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule establishes that a monk incurs an offense entailing confession (*pācittiya*) if he intentionally causes anxiety or vexation to another monk [Hüsken 1997]. In an examination of Vinaya exoneration formulas, Ute Hüsken observes that the sole basis for exemption from liability (*anāpatti*) under this rule is when the monk acts without the intention to cause distress or trouble to another [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the text has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Curated parallels for the rule are found in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Pācittiya 77) and the *Bhikkhu Parivāra*, with a counterpart in the nuns' discipline at *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* Pācittiya 155. Extensive cross-tradition parallels survive in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan within the monastic codes of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and Upaliparipṛcchā lineages. Text-reuse data computed by DharmaNexus demonstrates that the text shares substantial stock phrasing and procedural segments with other Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga rules—most notably Pācittiyas 74, 75, 78, and 23—as well as subcommentarial reuse in the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
